briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Tax Relief Momentum Builds in Lansing as National Rescheduling and Psychedelics Keep Moving Forward
briefs.top: Michigan's cannabis operators are getting real political air cover this week as gubernatorial politics turn the 24% wholesale tax into a 2026 campaign flashpoint, with a bipartisan repeal bill also on the table. Nationally, courts just upheld medical marijuana's Schedule III status, Compass Pathways keeps pushing psilocybin toward FDA approval, and MSOs are consolidating aggressively — all signs the bigger picture is bending toward opportunity.

local.text: GOP gubernatorial nominee John James is campaigning hard on a pledge to 'repeal or sharply reduce' Michigan's 24% wholesale marijuana tax and is pulling in cannabis-industry donor cash as a result, with MiCIA's executive director saying operators are 'pretty united' around him — a real shot at relief if he wins in November.

A Republican state representative has introduced House Bill 6224 to repeal the 24% wholesale tax outright, adding a second legislative track alongside the MiCIA court appeal — and lawmakers from both parties are now backing repeal proposals, arguing the levy has generated less revenue than promised.

Despite the new tax, Michigan demand hasn't cratered: the state posted $1.48 billion in adult-use sales through the first half of 2026 alone, pushing the all-time market total past $16.5 billion — proof the country's second-largest cannabis market is still drawing customers even as prices stay near record lows.

Muskegon's Fields Cannary is targeting a fall opening for a dispensary paired with a full-service restaurant — a hospitality-forward format that pushes the retail experience further than most Michigan operators have attempted, and a template worth watching for Ann Arbor and Detroit brands.

While the wholesale tax has forced Higher Love to close five of nine Upper Peninsula stores, three-location operator Rize is showing the playbook forward — sustaining growth by negotiating cost-sharing arrangements that split the tax burden with suppliers instead of absorbing it alone.

national.text: The D.C. Circuit just handed the industry a win: on Sept. 9 the court left the medical marijuana rescheduling order in effect, rejecting a challenge and holding that opponents hadn't shown the reclassification to Schedule III was unlawful — clearing a path for continued §280E tax relief discussions.

Compass Pathways just named the recipients of its U.S. grant program to train healthcare providers on delivering COMP360 psilocybin therapy — building the clinical infrastructure needed ahead of an expected FDA decision, after the company already reported positive six-month durability data from its second Phase 3 trial.

MDMA therapy is getting a second act: after its 2024 FDA rejection, Lykos rebranded as Resilient Pharmaceuticals and resubmitted its New Drug Application in August 2026, leaning on new VA follow-up data and an independent audit rather than a full repeat Phase 3 trial.

Vireo Growth is on an acquisition tear — closing deals for FLUENT, C21, and PharmaCann while merging with Planet 13 — and posted Q2 revenue up 335% year-over-year to $209.3 million, a sign that scaled consolidation is very much alive even if headline MSO mega-mergers are quiet.

Curaleaf keeps expanding its footprint, opening its 76th Florida dispensary in Cutler Bay on September 1 — continued brick-and-mortar growth from one of the industry's biggest multistate operators even as public-market M&A stays cautious.
